origin.description: Reduce a character vector to one string, with an optional different separator before the last piece.
origin.usage: str_flatten(string, collapse = "", last = NULL, na.rm = FALSE)

arguments.name: string
arguments.text: A character vector, or another vector that can be coerced to character.

arguments.name: collapse
arguments.text: A single string inserted between pieces. The default is empty.

arguments.name: last
arguments.text: A single string used before the final piece, or NULL to keep collapse there too.

arguments.name: na.rm
arguments.text: When TRUE, missing values are removed first. When FALSE, any missing value makes the result missing.

origin.details: The result is one string no matter how long the input is. last is used only when at least two pieces remain. NULL and a vector of only missing values with na.rm TRUE both become an empty string.
origin.example:
cat(paste0("str_flatten(letters[1:3], \", \", \" and \") returns ", str_flatten(letters[1:3], ", ", " and "), ".\n"))
cat(paste0("str_flatten(letters[1:2], \", \", \", and \") returns ", str_flatten(letters[1:2], ", ", ", and "), ".\n"))

translation.description: Join one vector with stringi.stri_flatten, after building the last piece with stringi.stri_c.

arguments.name: string
arguments.text: A string, NA, or a list of those. None is an empty vector.

arguments.name: last
arguments.text: None keeps collapse before the last piece. A string replaces that final separator.

arguments.name: na_rm
arguments.text: R's na.rm. True drops missing values before joining.

translation.details: A missing value is stringi._na.NA. With na_rm false, one missing value makes the only result missing. The return value is a list of length 1.
translation.value: A list of one string, or one NA.
translation.example:
from stringr.join import str_flatten
print("str_flatten(letters[1:3], \", \", \" and \") returns " + str_flatten(list("abc"), ", ", " and ")[0] + ".")
print("str_flatten(letters[1:2], \", \", \", and \") returns " + str_flatten(list("ab"), ", ", ", and ")[0] + ".")
